Academic|Advanced.example: Our hypothesis turned out to be completely wrong.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: an idea you test to see if it is true

Academic|Advanced.example: There is little empirical support for that claim.

Academic|Advanced.example: The reviewers criticised her methodology, not her results.

Academic|Advanced.translation: The reviewers found fault with how she ran the study, not with what she found.

Academic|Advanced.example: The essay is interesting but not very coherent.

Academic|Advanced.translation: The essay has good ideas, but they do not hang together well.

Academic|Advanced.example: He could not substantiate any of his claims.

Academic|Advanced.translation: He was unable to back up a single one of his claims with proof.

Academic|Advanced.example: Your summary misses an important nuance in the argument.

Academic|Advanced.translation: Your summary leaves out a fine but important shade of meaning in the argument.

Academic|Advanced.example: That discovery shifted the paradigm in the field.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: a whole way of thinking that guides a field
Academic|Advanced.translation: That finding changed the dominant way of thinking in the discipline.

Academic|Advanced.example: The journal only accepts rigorous studies.

Academic|Advanced.example: Two later studies corroborate her original result.

Academic|Advanced.translation: Two studies done afterwards back up what she found first.

Academic|Advanced.example: The whole chapter rests on a shaky premise.

Academic|Advanced.translation: The entire chapter is built on an assumption that does not hold up.

Academic|Advanced.example: Her book changed the discourse around climate policy.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: serious discussion or writing on a subject
Academic|Advanced.translation: Her book altered the way people write and talk about climate policy.

Academic|Advanced.example: The wording of the question is ambiguous.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: able to be understood in more than one way
Academic|Advanced.translation: The question is phrased so that it could mean two different things.

Academic|Advanced.example: The final chapter is a synthesis of both traditions.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: combining separate ideas into one whole
Academic|Advanced.translation: The last chapter brings both traditions together into one account.

Academic|Advanced.example: That is a plausible explanation, but we need data.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: believable, though not proven
Academic|Advanced.translation: The explanation sounds believable, yet we still need figures to check it.

Academic|Advanced.example: There is an inherent bias in how the sample was chosen.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: existing as a basic part of something
Academic|Advanced.translation: The way the sample was picked carries a bias built into it.

Academic|Advanced.example: His figures did not survive close scrutiny.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: very close and careful examination
Academic|Advanced.translation: When his numbers were examined carefully, they fell apart.

Academic|Advanced.example: The introduction should delineate the scope of the study.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: to describe or mark out something clearly
Academic|Advanced.translation: The opening section ought to set out clearly what the study covers.

Academic|Advanced.example: The cut-off point looks completely arbitrary to me.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: chosen with no clear reason behind it
Academic|Advanced.translation: As far as I can see, the cut-off was picked for no particular reason.

Academic|Advanced.example: These are only preliminary findings, so be careful.
Academic|Advanced.meaning: done first, before the main work
Academic|Advanced.translation: These results are early ones, so treat them with caution.

Academic|Advanced.example: You cannot extrapolate from such a small sample.

Academic|Advanced.translation: A sample that small does not let you draw wider conclusions.

Academic|Beginner.example: I have to study for my history test tonight.

Academic|Beginner.translation: The exam turned out to be simpler than I thought it would be.

Academic|Beginner.translation: She allowed me to copy what she had written down during the lecture.

Academic|Beginner.translation: Put your name in the space at the top of the page.

Academic|Beginner.translation: Show me one case of it so the idea is clearer to me.

Academic|Intermediate.example: I did some research before writing the essay.

Academic|Intermediate.example: We studied his theory about how memory works.

Travel|Beginner.meaning: the small object that opens a door
Travel|Beginner.translation: I forgot the door opener on the table in my hotel room.

Travel|Beginner.example: I changed some money at the airport before we left.
Travel|Beginner.meaning: the coins and notes you pay with
Travel|Beginner.translation: I swapped my cash for the local kind at the airport.

Travel|Beginner.example: We want to visit the old castle tomorrow morning.
Travel|Beginner.meaning: to go and see a place or a person
Travel|Beginner.translation: We plan to go and see the old castle in the morning.

Travel|Beginner.example: She brought her camera to take pictures of the harbour.
Travel|Beginner.meaning: a small machine for taking photos
Travel|Beginner.translation: She carried a photo-taking device to get pictures of the harbour.

Travel|Beginner.example: We are going on holiday for two weeks in July.
Travel|Beginner.meaning: time away from work or school for travel and rest
Travel|Beginner.translation: We will be away resting and travelling for two weeks in July.

Travel|Intermediate.example: Have your boarding pass ready before you reach the gate.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: the card that lets you get on a plane
Travel|Intermediate.translation: Get the card that lets you onto the plane out before the gate.

Travel|Intermediate.example: Our luggage did not arrive with us in Lisbon.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: all the bags you take on a journey
Travel|Intermediate.translation: Our bags failed to turn up in Lisbon when we did.

Travel|Intermediate.example: The departure time on the screen changed to nine forty.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: the act of leaving on a journey
Travel|Intermediate.translation: The screen now says the plane leaves at nine forty instead.

Travel|Intermediate.example: We will call you as soon as we hear the arrival announcement.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: the moment you get to a place
Travel|Intermediate.translation: We will phone you the second they announce that the plane has landed.

Travel|Intermediate.example: There was a two-hour delay because of the storm.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: a wait that makes something happen later than planned
Travel|Intermediate.translation: The storm made everything happen two hours later than planned.

Travel|Intermediate.example: They stopped me at customs and looked inside my suitcase.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: the place where officials check what you bring into a country
Travel|Intermediate.translation: The border officials pulled me aside and searched my suitcase.

Travel|Intermediate.example: I made a reservation for two nights under my last name.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: an arrangement to keep a room or seat for you
Travel|Intermediate.translation: I booked a room for two nights, and it is listed under my surname.

Travel|Intermediate.example: We can check in at the hotel any time after two o'clock.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: to register your arrival at a hotel or airport
Travel|Intermediate.translation: The hotel will register our arrival from two o'clock onwards.

Travel|Intermediate.example: The local currency is much weaker than it was last year.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: the type of money a country uses
Travel|Intermediate.translation: The money used here is worth far less than it was a year ago.

Travel|Intermediate.example: My guidebook says the cathedral closes at five.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: a book with information for visitors to a place
Travel|Intermediate.translation: According to my visitor information book, the cathedral shuts at five.

Travel|Intermediate.example: I bought a small wooden bird as a souvenir from Prague.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: something you buy to remember a place by
Travel|Intermediate.translation: I got a little wooden bird in Prague to help me remember the trip.

Travel|Intermediate.example: We spent the whole morning sightseeing in the old town.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: visiting interesting places as a tourist
Travel|Intermediate.translation: We looked around the interesting parts of the old town all morning.

Travel|Intermediate.example: Accommodation near the station is cheaper than in the centre.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: a place to stay while you travel
Travel|Intermediate.translation: Places to stay by the station cost less than ones downtown.

Travel|Intermediate.example: If this train is late, I will miss my connection in Zurich.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: a second flight or train you change onto
Travel|Intermediate.translation: A late train means I won't catch the onward service in Zurich.

Travel|Intermediate.example: I only booked a one-way ticket because I am not sure when I will come back.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: going in a single direction, with no return
Travel|Intermediate.translation: I bought a ticket for the outward trip only, since my return date is uncertain.

Travel|Intermediate.example: I always ask for a seat by the aisle so I can stretch my legs.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: the walkway between rows of seats
Travel|Intermediate.translation: I request a seat next to the walkway so I have room to stretch.

Travel|Intermediate.example: The fare from the airport into town is about twenty euros.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: the price you pay to travel
Travel|Intermediate.translation: It costs roughly twenty euros to travel from the airport into town.

Travel|Intermediate.example: We made a short detour to see the waterfall on the way.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: a longer route taken instead of the direct one
Travel|Intermediate.translation: We went a slightly longer way so we could see the waterfall.

Travel|Intermediate.example: Travel insurance covered the doctor's bill in Greece.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: money protection you buy in case something goes wrong
Travel|Intermediate.translation: The protection policy we bought paid for the doctor in Greece.

Travel|Intermediate.example: The clock tower is the easiest landmark to find in this city.
Travel|Intermediate.meaning: a famous building or feature that is easy to recognise
Travel|Intermediate.translation: The clock tower is the simplest well-known feature to spot here.
